natural_body: 40% SMB discount: signup +31%, revenue +18%, but retention -12%; no renewal.

first.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down this quarter, and two independent inherited memories (31, 86) point to onboarding simplification as a durable, low-risk lever for exactly these metrics, so I verify those two source records before committing. Promotional_pricing is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but memory_73 shows a similar SMB discount produced short-term signup/revenue gains offset by a 12% retention drop and no renewal—i.e., it looks like sustainable-revenue-negative, so I'm flagging that risk and not choosing it this week despite competitive pressure. Referral_incentive (memory_57) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) address different funnel stages and don't target the current activation/onboarding regression as directly. With only one experiment slot, I'm running simplify_onboarding as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, since I've only verified 2 of the relevant memories and want to confirm the original onboarding results generalize to the current cohort before scaling, especially while competitive dynamics are shifting SMB behavior.
